extracted.intended_audience: state agency rulewriters, attorneys, and members of the public seeking information about the Texas Administrative Code
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level official overview of the Texas Administrative Code (TAC): its statutory basis, organization into titles, electronic availability, and the role (and limits) of the Secretary of State regarding the TAC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of State does not interpret or enforce the Texas Administrative Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of State does not interpret or enforce the Texas Administrative Code. If you need interpretation of a current rule, please contact the agency that promulgated the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should not rely on the Secretary of State for legal interpretation or enforcement of TAC provisions; instead they must consult the specific agency that adopted the rule for interpretation, enforcement questions, or guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: TAC is a compilation of all state agency rules and is organized by titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Texas Administrative Code (TAC) is a compilation of all state agency rules in Texas. There are 17 titles in the TAC. Each title represents a subject category and related agencies are assigned to the appropriate title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When locating or drafting rules, expect rules to be grouped by subject area under one of the 17 titles; ensure rules are placed/consulted under the correct title corresponding to the subject/agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory responsibility to compile, index, and publish the TAC
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1977 the TAC was created by the Texas Legislature under the Administrative Code Act (Government Code, §§2002.051-2002.056). The Legislature directed the Office of the Secretary of State to compile, index, and cause to be published the Texas Administrative Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of the Secretary of State performs compilation, indexing, and publication duties pursuant to statute; rule drafters and users should understand the TAC's official publication role is statutory and centralized at SOS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical rulemaking coordination and legal framework
rubrics_metrics.description: State agency rule writers, in cooperation with the Office of the Secretary of State, began organization and systematic dissemination of state agency rules in 1975 with the passage of the Administrative Procedure and Texas Register Act (Government Code, §2001 and §2002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TAC and Texas Register arise from the Administrative Procedure and Texas Register Act; users researching rule history or procedure should consult the Texas Register and relevant statutory provisions for procedural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic availability requirement and value-added service policy (HB 2304)
rubrics_metrics.description: HB 2304 (1995) allows the Secretary of State to make the TAC available through the web site and to charge for value-added services available through the web site. HB 2304 also mandated that the TAC be made available in an electronic format at no charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TAC must be provided electronically free of charge (complimentary service available via 'View TAC'), while the SOS may offer and charge for additional value-added online services (e.g., enhanced search or copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online search coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Search the Texas Administrative Code (includes information in effect on January 1, 1999 - current).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TAC search tool covers material effective from January 1, 1999 to the present; for materials prior to 1999 or historical archives, consult the Texas Register Back Issue Archive or other library resources (e.g., University of North Texas Libraries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided SOS resources for access and related materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOS site provides links/resources such as 'View the current Texas Administrative Code', 'Search the Texas Administrative Code', 'Texas Register', and back-issue archives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accessing rules or rulemaking information, use the SOS-provided links (View TAC, search, Texas Register) and external library/archive resources referenced on the page to obtain current or historical rule texts and notices.
